results.question: How many vehicles are currently available?

results.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM vehicles WHERE status = 'available'

results.question: List all branch offices and the city they are in. Show the branch name and city.
results.sql: SELECT name AS branch_name, city FROM locations ORDER BY city, name
results.gold_sql: SELECT name, city FROM locations

results.question: How many Toyota cars do we own?
results.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) as toyota_count FROM vehicles WHERE make = 'Toyota'
results.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM vehicles WHERE make = 'Toyota'

results.question: Which vehicles are currently in maintenance? Show make, model and license plate.
results.sql: SELECT DISTINCT v.make, v.model, v.license_plate FROM vehicles v INNER JOIN maintenance_records mr ON v.id = mr.vehicle_id WHERE mr.completed = false ORDER BY v.license_plate
results.gold_sql: SELECT make, model, license_plate FROM vehicles WHERE status = 'maintenance'

results.question: Câți clienți sunt înregistrați în total?
results.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) as total_clients FROM clients
results.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM clients

results.question: Show the five most expensive vehicles by daily rate. Show make, model and daily rate.
results.sql: SELECT make, model, daily_rate FROM vehicles ORDER BY daily_rate DESC LIMIT 5
results.gold_sql: SELECT make, model, daily_rate FROM vehicles ORDER BY daily_rate DESC LIMIT 5

results.question: What is the average salary of employees per branch? Show the branch name and the average salary.
results.sql: SELECT l.name AS branch_name, AVG(e.salary) AS average_salary FROM employees e JOIN locations l ON e.location_id = l.id GROUP BY l.id, l.name ORDER BY l.name
results.gold_sql: SELECT l.name, AVG(e.salary) AS avg_salary FROM employees e JOIN locations l ON e.location_id = l.id GROUP BY l.name

results.question: How many vehicles are there in each category? Show the category name and the number of vehicles.
results.sql: SELECT vc.name, COUNT(v.id) as vehicle_count FROM vehicles v JOIN vehicle_categories vc ON v.category_id = vc.id GROUP BY vc.name ORDER BY vc.name
results.gold_sql: SELECT c.name, COUNT(*) AS vehicle_count FROM vehicles v JOIN vehicle_categories c ON v.category_id = c.id GROUP BY c.name

results.question: What is the total revenue from completed payments?
results.sql: SELECT SUM(amount) as total_revenue FROM payments WHERE status = 'completed'
results.gold_sql: SELECT SUM(amount) AS total FROM payments WHERE status = 'completed'

results.question: Show total revenue from completed payments by location. Show the location name and the revenue.
results.sql: SELECT l.name as location_name, SUM(p.amount) as revenue FROM payments p JOIN reservations r ON p.reservation_id = r.id JOIN locations l ON r.pickup_location = l.id WHERE p.status = 'completed' GROUP BY l.id, l.name ORDER BY l.name
results.gold_sql: SELECT l.name, SUM(p.amount) AS revenue FROM payments p JOIN reservations r ON p.reservation_id = r.id JOIN locations l ON r.pickup_location = l.id WHERE p.status = 'completed' GROUP BY l.name

results.question: What is the average rating for each vehicle category? Show the category name and the average rating.
results.sql: SELECT vc.name AS category_name, AVG(r.rating)::NUMERIC(3,2) AS average_rating FROM reviews r JOIN reservations res ON r.reservation_id = res.id JOIN vehicles v ON res.vehicle_id = v.id JOIN vehicle_categories vc ON v.category_id = vc.id GROUP BY vc.id, vc.name ORDER BY vc.name
results.gold_sql: SELECT c.name, AVG(rv.rating) AS avg_rating FROM reviews rv JOIN reservations r ON rv.reservation_id = r.id JOIN vehicles v ON r.vehicle_id = v.id JOIN vehicle_categories c ON v.category_id = c.id GROUP BY c.name

results.question: Which vehicle categories have more than fifteen vehicles? Show the category name and the count.
results.sql: SELECT vc.name, COUNT(v.id) as count FROM vehicle_categories vc JOIN vehicles v ON vc.id = v.category_id GROUP BY vc.name HAVING COUNT(v.id) > 15 ORDER BY count DESC
results.gold_sql: SELECT c.name, COUNT(*) AS n FROM vehicles v JOIN vehicle_categories c ON v.category_id = c.id GROUP BY c.name HAVING COUNT(*) > 15

results.question: How much have we spent on maintenance per maintenance type? Show the maintenance type and the total cost.
results.sql: SELECT maintenance_type, SUM(cost) as total_cost FROM maintenance_records GROUP BY maintenance_type ORDER BY total_cost DESC
results.gold_sql: SELECT maintenance_type, SUM(cost) AS total FROM maintenance_records GROUP BY maintenance_type

results.question: Care sunt veniturile totale din plățile finalizate, pe fiecare metodă de plată? Arată metoda de plată și totalul.
results.sql: SELECT payment_method, SUM(amount) as total_revenue FROM payments WHERE status = 'completed' GROUP BY payment_method ORDER BY total_revenue DESC
results.gold_sql: SELECT payment_method, SUM(amount) AS total FROM payments WHERE status = 'completed' GROUP BY payment_method

results.question: List the reservations picked up in Miami. Show reservation id, pickup date and return date.
results.sql: SELECT r.id, r.pickup_date, r.return_date FROM reservations r JOIN locations l ON r.pickup_location = l.id WHERE l.city = 'Miami' ORDER BY r.id
results.gold_sql: SELECT r.id, r.pickup_date, r.return_date FROM reservations r JOIN locations l ON r.pickup_location = l.id WHERE l.city = 'Miami'

results.question: Show each client's first name, last name and the number of reservations they made, including clients with none.
results.sql: SELECT c.first_name, c.last_name, COUNT(r.id) as reservation_count FROM clients c LEFT JOIN reservations r ON c.id = r.client_id GROUP BY c.id, c.first_name, c.last_name ORDER BY c.last_name, c.first_name
results.gold_sql: SELECT c.first_name, c.last_name, COUNT(r.id) AS reservations FROM clients c LEFT JOIN reservations r ON r.client_id = c.id GROUP BY c.id, c.first_name, c.last_name

results.question: Which employees work at the Downtown Hub? Show first name, last name and role.
results.sql: SELECT e.first_name, e.last_name, e.role FROM employees e JOIN locations l ON e.location_id = l.id WHERE l.name = 'Downtown Hub' ORDER BY e.last_name, e.first_name
results.gold_sql: SELECT e.first_name, e.last_name, e.role FROM employees e JOIN locations l ON e.location_id = l.id WHERE l.name = 'Downtown Hub'

results.question: Which reservations have no payment recorded against them? Show reservation id, pickup date and total cost.
results.sql: SELECT r.id as reservation_id, r.pickup_date, r.total_cost FROM reservations r WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM payments p WHERE p.reservation_id = r.id) ORDER BY r.id
results.gold_sql: SELECT r.id, r.pickup_date, r.total_cost FROM reservations r WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM payments p WHERE p.reservation_id = r.id)

results.question: Show all reviews with a rating of 1. Show the rating, the comment, and the make and model of the vehicle.
results.sql: SELECT r.rating, r.comment, v.make, v.model FROM reviews r JOIN reservations res ON r.reservation_id = res.id JOIN vehicles v ON res.vehicle_id = v.id WHERE r.rating = 1 ORDER BY r.id
results.gold_sql: SELECT rv.rating, rv.comment, v.make, v.model FROM reviews rv JOIN reservations r ON rv.reservation_id = r.id JOIN vehicles v ON r.vehicle_id = v.id WHERE rv.rating = 1

results.question: Which vehicles have a daily rate above the average daily rate? Show make, model and daily rate.
results.sql: SELECT make, model, daily_rate FROM vehicles WHERE daily_rate > (SELECT AVG(daily_rate) FROM vehicles) ORDER BY daily_rate DESC
results.gold_sql: SELECT make, model, daily_rate FROM vehicles WHERE daily_rate > (SELECT AVG(daily_rate) FROM vehicles)

results.question: Which clients have the highest total reservation cost? Show the top ten as first name, last name and the total.
results.sql: SELECT c.first_name, c.last_name, SUM(r.total_cost) as total_cost FROM clients c JOIN reservations r ON c.id = r.client_id GROUP BY c.id, c.first_name, c.last_name ORDER BY total_cost DESC LIMIT 10
results.gold_sql: SELECT c.first_name, c.last_name, SUM(r.total_cost) AS spent FROM clients c JOIN reservations r ON r.client_id = c.id GROUP BY c.id, c.first_name, c.last_name ORDER BY spent DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10

results.question: Find the branch with the highest total revenue from completed payments. Show the branch name and its total revenue.
results.sql: SELECT l.name as branch_name, SUM(p.amount) as total_revenue FROM payments p JOIN reservations r ON p.reservation_id = r.id JOIN vehicles v ON r.vehicle_id = v.id JOIN locations l ON v.location_id = l.id WHERE p.status = 'completed' GROUP BY l.id, l.name ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 1
results.gold_sql: SELECT l.name, SUM(p.amount) AS revenue FROM payments p JOIN reservations r ON p.reservation_id = r.id JOIN locations l ON r.pickup_location = l.id WHERE p.status = 'completed' GROUP BY l.name ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 1

results.question: Which vehicles have had more than three maintenance records? Show make, model and license plate.
results.sql: SELECT v.make, v.model, v.license_plate, COUNT(mr.id) as maintenance_count FROM vehicles v LEFT JOIN maintenance_records mr ON v.id = mr.vehicle_id GROUP BY v.id, v.make, v.model, v.license_plate HAVING COUNT(mr.id) > 3 ORDER BY v.make, v.model, v.license_plate
results.gold_sql: SELECT v.make, v.model, v.license_plate FROM vehicles v WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM maintenance_records m WHERE m.vehicle_id = v.id) > 3

results.question: List clients who have never left a review. Show first and last name.
results.sql: SELECT c.first_name, c.last_name FROM clients c WHERE c.id NOT IN (SELECT DISTINCT r.client_id FROM reviews rev JOIN reservations r ON rev.reservation_id = r.id) ORDER BY c.last_name, c.first_name
results.gold_sql:
SELECT c.first_name, c.last_name FROM clients c WHERE NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM reservations r
  JOIN reviews rv ON rv.reservation_id = r.id
  WHERE r.client_id = c.id
)

results.question: For each branch, show the highest paid employee as branch name, first name, last name and salary.
results.sql: WITH ranked_employees AS (SELECT e.location_id, l.name AS branch_name, e.first_name, e.last_name, e.salary, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY e.location_id ORDER BY e.salary DESC) AS rank FROM employees e JOIN locations l ON e.location_id = l.id) SELECT branch_name, first_name, last_name, salary FROM ranked_employees WHERE rank = 1 ORDER BY branch_name
results.gold_sql:
SELECT name, first_name, last_name, salary FROM (
  SELECT l.name, e.first_name, e.last_name, e.salary,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY l.id ORDER BY e.salary DESC) AS rn
  FROM employees e JOIN locations l ON e.location_id = l.id
) t WHERE rn = 1

results.question: Show monthly reservation counts for 2024, as the first day of each month and the count.
results.gold_sql: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', pickup_date) AS month, COUNT(*) AS n FROM reservations WHERE pickup_date >= DATE '2024-01-01' AND pickup_date < DATE '2025-01-01' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

results.question: Care sunt cei mai buni clienți?
results.sql: SELECT c.id, c.first_name, c.last_name, c.email, COUNT(r.id) as number_of_rentals, SUM(r.total_cost) as total_revenue FROM clients c LEFT JOIN reservations r ON c.id = r.client_id GROUP BY c.id, c.first_name, c.last_name, c.email ORDER BY total_revenue DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 20

results.question: Show me the good vehicles.
How is the business doing?
Hello, what can you do?
For each vehicle make, show the make, the total revenue from completed payments on that make's reservations, and the total maintenance cost recorded for that make's vehicles.
results.sql: SELECT v.make, COALESCE(SUM(payment_sums.revenue), 0) as total_revenue, COALESCE(SUM(maintenance_sums.cost), 0) as total_maintenance_cost FROM vehicles v LEFT JOIN (SELECT r.vehicle_id, SUM(CASE WHEN p.status = 'completed' THEN p.amount ELSE 0 END) as revenue FROM reservations r LEFT JOIN payments p ON r.id = p.reservation_id GROUP BY r.vehicle_id) payment_sums ON v.id = payment_sums.vehicle_id LEFT JOIN (SELECT vehicle_id, SUM(cost) as cost FROM maintenance_records GROUP BY vehicle_id) maintenance_sums ON v.id = maintenance_sums.vehicle_id GROUP BY v.make ORDER BY v.make
results.gold_sql:
WITH rev AS (
  SELECT v.make, SUM(p.amount) AS revenue
  FROM payments p
  JOIN reservations r ON r.id = p.reservation_id
  JOIN vehicles v ON v.id = r.vehicle_id
  WHERE p.status = 'completed'
  GROUP BY v.make),
mnt AS (
  SELECT v.make, SUM(m.cost) AS maintenance_cost
  FROM maintenance_records m
  JOIN vehicles v ON v.id = m.vehicle_id
  GROUP BY v.make)
SELECT rev.make, rev.revenue, mnt.maintenance_cost FROM rev JOIN mnt ON mnt.make = rev.make

results.question: Which vehicles are double-booked at least ten times — pairs of two different reservations on the same vehicle, neither of them cancelled or a no-show, whose date ranges share at least one calendar day (pickup and return days inclusive)? Show make, model, license plate and the number of such pairs.
results.sql: SELECT v.make, v.model, v.license_plate, COUNT(*) as overlap_pairs FROM reservations r1 JOIN reservations r2 ON r1.vehicle_id = r2.vehicle_id AND r1.id < r2.id AND r1.pickup_date <= r2.return_date AND r1.return_date >= r2.pickup_date JOIN vehicles v ON r1.vehicle_id = v.id WHERE r1.status NOT IN ('cancelled', 'no_show') AND r2.status NOT IN ('cancelled', 'no_show') GROUP BY v.id, v.make, v.model, v.license_plate HAVING COUNT(*) >= 10 ORDER BY overlap_pairs DESC
results.gold_sql:
SELECT v.make, v.model, v.license_plate, COUNT(*) AS overlapping_pairs FROM reservations a JOIN reservations b
  ON b.vehicle_id = a.vehicle_id AND a.id < b.id
 AND a.pickup_date <= b.return_date AND b.pickup_date <= a.return_date
JOIN vehicles v ON v.id = a.vehicle_id WHERE a.status NOT IN ('cancelled', 'no_show')
  AND b.status NOT IN ('cancelled', 'no_show')
GROUP BY v.id, v.make, v.model, v.license_plate HAVING COUNT(*) >= 10

results.question: Which vehicles were idle for at least 340 days of 2024? A day is idle when it is not covered by any reservation of that vehicle that is not cancelled and not a no-show; pickup and return days count as covered, and each calendar day counts at most once per vehicle even when reservations overlap. Show the license plate and the number of idle days.
results.sql: WITH valid_reservations AS (SELECT vehicle_id, pickup_date, return_date FROM reservations WHERE status NOT IN ('cancelled', 'no_show') AND return_date >= '2024-01-01' AND pickup_date <= '2024-12-31'), covered_days AS (SELECT DISTINCT v.vehicle_id, d.day FROM valid_reservations v CROSS JOIN LATERAL (SELECT generate_series(GREATEST(v.pickup_date, '2024-01-01'::date), LEAST(v.return_date, '2024-12-31'::date), interval '1 day')::date AS day) d), vehicles_idle_days AS (SELECT v.id, v.license_plate, 366 - COALESCE(COUNT(DISTINCT cd.day), 0) as idle_days FROM vehicles v LEFT JOIN covered_days cd ON v.id = cd.vehicle_id GROUP BY v.id, v.license_plate) SELECT license_plate, idle_days FROM vehicles_idle_days WHERE idle_days >= 340 ORDER BY idle_days DESC
results.gold_sql:
WITH days AS (
  SELECT v.id AS vehicle_id, v.license_plate, d::date AS day
  FROM vehicles v
  CROSS JOIN generate_series(DATE '2024-01-01', DATE '2024-12-31', INTERVAL '1 day') d),
covered AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT r.vehicle_id, d.day
  FROM reservations r
  JOIN days d ON d.vehicle_id = r.vehicle_id
   AND d.day BETWEEN r.pickup_date AND r.return_date
  WHERE r.status NOT IN ('cancelled', 'no_show'))
SELECT dy.license_plate, COUNT(*) AS idle_days FROM days dy LEFT JOIN covered c ON c.vehicle_id = dy.vehicle_id AND c.day = dy.day WHERE c.vehicle_id IS NULL GROUP BY dy.vehicle_id, dy.license_plate HAVING COUNT(*) >= 340

results.question: For each month of 2024, show the month as a date (the first day of the month), the revenue from completed payments received in that month (by payment date), and the percentage change versus the same month of 2023, rounded to two decimals.
results.sql: WITH payments_2024 AS (SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', payment_date)::date as month, EXTRACT(MONTH FROM payment_date)::int as month_num, SUM(amount) as revenue FROM payments WHERE status = 'completed' AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM payment_date) = 2024 GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', payment_date), EXTRACT(MONTH FROM payment_date)), payments_2023 AS (SELECT EXTRACT(MONTH FROM payment_date)::int as month_num, SUM(amount) as revenue FROM payments WHERE status = 'completed' AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM payment_date) = 2023 GROUP BY EXTRACT(MONTH FROM payment_date)) SELECT p24.month, p24.revenue, ROUND(((p24.revenue - COALESCE(p23.revenue, 0)) / NULLIF(p23.revenue, 0) * 100)::numeric, 2) as pct_change FROM payments_2024 p24 LEFT JOIN payments_2023 p23 ON p24.month_num = p23.month_num ORDER BY p24.month
results.gold_sql:
WITH m AS (
  SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', payment_date)::date AS month, SUM(amount) AS revenue
  FROM payments WHERE status = 'completed' GROUP BY 1)
SELECT a.month, a.revenue,
       ROUND(100.0 * (a.revenue - b.revenue) / b.revenue, 2) AS yoy_pct
FROM m a JOIN m b ON b.month = a.month - INTERVAL '1 year' WHERE a.month >= DATE '2024-01-01' AND a.month < DATE '2025-01-01' ORDER BY a.month

results.question: Show the three-month trailing moving average of monthly revenue from completed payments - the mean of that month and the two preceding months - for every month of 2024. The average must be computed over the full payment history, so January 2024 averages November 2023, December 2023 and January 2024. Show the month as a date, that month's revenue, and the moving average rounded to two decimals.
results.sql: WITH monthly_revenue AS (SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', payment_date)::date AS month, SUM(amount) AS revenue FROM payments WHERE status = 'completed' AND payment_date >= '2023-11-01' GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', payment_date)) SELECT month, revenue, ROUND(AVG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)::numeric, 2) AS moving_average FROM monthly_revenue WHERE month >= '2024-01-01' ORDER BY month
results.gold_sql:
WITH m AS (
  SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', payment_date)::date AS month, SUM(amount) AS revenue
  FROM payments WHERE status = 'completed' GROUP BY 1),
ma AS (
  SELECT month, revenue,
         ROUND(AVG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month
               ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), 2) AS moving_avg
  FROM m)
SELECT month, revenue, moving_avg FROM ma WHERE month >= DATE '2024-01-01' AND month < DATE '2025-01-01' ORDER BY month

results.question: For each branch, show the branch name and the revenue from completed payments split into three separate columns by payment method - credit card, debit card and cash. Attribute each payment to the pickup branch of its reservation.
results.sql: SELECT l.name AS branch_name, COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN p.payment_method = 'credit_card' THEN p.amount ELSE 0 END), 0) AS credit_card_revenue, COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN p.payment_method = 'debit_card' THEN p.amount ELSE 0 END), 0) AS debit_card_revenue, COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN p.payment_method = 'cash' THEN p.amount ELSE 0 END), 0) AS cash_revenue FROM payments p JOIN reservations r ON p.reservation_id = r.id JOIN locations l ON r.pickup_location = l.id WHERE p.status = 'completed' GROUP BY l.id, l.name ORDER BY l.name
results.gold_sql:
SELECT l.name,
       COALESCE(SUM(p.amount) FILTER (WHERE p.payment_method = 'credit_card'), 0) AS credit_card,
       COALESCE(SUM(p.amount) FILTER (WHERE p.payment_method = 'debit_card'), 0) AS debit_card,
       COALESCE(SUM(p.amount) FILTER (WHERE p.payment_method = 'cash'), 0) AS cash
FROM payments p JOIN reservations r ON r.id = p.reservation_id JOIN locations l ON l.id = r.pickup_location WHERE p.status = 'completed' GROUP BY l.name

results.question: Pentru fiecare categorie de vehicule, care este costul median al rezervărilor finalizate, calculat ca mediană interpolată (media celor două valori din mijloc când numărul de rezervări este par) și rotunjit la două zecimale? Arată numele categoriei și mediana.
results.sql: SELECT vc.name, ROUND(PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY r.total_cost)::numeric, 2) as median_cost FROM reservations r JOIN vehicles v ON r.vehicle_id = v.id JOIN vehicle_categories vc ON v.category_id = vc.id WHERE r.status = 'completed' GROUP BY vc.name ORDER BY vc.name
results.gold_sql:
SELECT c.name,
       ROUND((PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY r.total_cost))::numeric, 2) AS median_cost
FROM reservations r JOIN vehicles v ON v.id = r.vehicle_id JOIN vehicle_categories c ON c.id = v.category_id WHERE r.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.name

results.question: For each vehicle category, show the category name and the revenue per rental day, defined as the total amount of completed payments divided by the total number of rental days (return date minus pickup date) of the reservations those payments belong to, rounded to two decimals. Divide the two totals - do not average per-reservation daily rates.
results.sql: SELECT vc.name, ROUND(SUM(p.amount)::numeric / SUM((r.return_date - r.pickup_date))::numeric, 2) AS revenue_per_rental_day FROM vehicle_categories vc JOIN vehicles v ON vc.id = v.category_id JOIN reservations r ON v.id = r.vehicle_id JOIN payments p ON r.id = p.reservation_id WHERE p.status = 'completed' GROUP BY vc.id, vc.name ORDER BY vc.name
results.gold_sql:
SELECT c.name,
       ROUND(SUM(p.amount) / SUM(r.return_date - r.pickup_date), 2) AS revenue_per_day
FROM payments p JOIN reservations r ON r.id = p.reservation_id JOIN vehicles v ON v.id = r.vehicle_id JOIN vehicle_categories c ON c.id = v.category_id WHERE p.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.name

results.question: For each branch, find the client who has spent the most in completed payments on reservations picked up at that branch. Show the branch name, the client's first name and last name, and the amount spent.
results.sql: WITH client_payments_by_branch AS (SELECT l.id as branch_id, l.name as branch_name, c.id as client_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, SUM(p.amount) as total_spent FROM reservations r JOIN locations l ON r.pickup_location = l.id JOIN clients c ON r.client_id = c.id JOIN payments p ON r.id = p.reservation_id WHERE p.status = 'completed' GROUP BY l.id, l.name, c.id, c.first_name, c.last_name), ranked_clients AS (SELECT branch_id, branch_name, client_id, first_name, last_name, total_spent, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY branch_id ORDER BY total_spent DESC) as rank FROM client_payments_by_branch) SELECT branch_name, first_name, last_name, total_spent FROM ranked_clients WHERE rank = 1 ORDER BY branch_name
results.gold_sql:
WITH spend AS (
  SELECT r.pickup_location, r.client_id, SUM(p.amount) AS spent
  FROM payments p
  JOIN reservations r ON r.id = p.reservation_id
  WHERE p.status = 'completed'
  GROUP BY r.pickup_location, r.client_id),
ranked AS (
  SELECT pickup_location, client_id, spent,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY pickup_location ORDER BY spent DESC) AS rn
  FROM spend)
SELECT l.name, c.first_name, c.last_name, rk.spent FROM ranked rk JOIN locations l ON l.id = rk.pickup_location JOIN clients c ON c.id = rk.client_id WHERE rk.rn = 1

results.question: Câți clienți au avut cel puțin o rezervare neanulată cu data de ridicare în 2023, dar nicio rezervare neanulată cu data de ridicare în 2024? Returnează un singur număr.
results.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT client_id) FROM reservations WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM pickup_date) = 2023 AND status != 'Cancelled' AND client_id NOT IN (SELECT DISTINCT client_id FROM reservations WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM pickup_date) = 2024 AND status != 'Cancelled')
results.gold_sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS churned_clients FROM (
  SELECT DISTINCT client_id FROM reservations
  WHERE status <> 'cancelled'
    AND pickup_date >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND pickup_date < DATE '2024-01-01'
  EXCEPT
  SELECT DISTINCT client_id FROM reservations
  WHERE status <> 'cancelled'
    AND pickup_date >= DATE '2024-01-01' AND pickup_date < DATE '2025-01-01') t

results.question: Consider the clients whose first non-cancelled reservation, by pickup date, was in 2022. How many such clients are there, how many of them made at least one non-cancelled reservation with a pickup date in 2023, and what percentage is that, rounded to two decimals? Return one row with the cohort size, the retained count and the retention percentage.
results.sql: WITH first_reservations AS (SELECT client_id, MIN(pickup_date) as first_pickup_date FROM reservations WHERE status != 'cancelled' GROUP BY client_id), cohort_2022 AS (SELECT client_id FROM first_reservations WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM first_pickup_date) = 2022), cohort_size_calc AS (SELECT COUNT(*) as cohort_size FROM cohort_2022), retained_2023 AS (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT r.client_id) as retained_count FROM reservations r JOIN cohort_2022 c ON r.client_id = c.client_id WHERE r.status != 'cancelled' AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM r.pickup_date) = 2023) SELECT cs.cohort_size, COALESCE(rt.retained_count, 0) as retained_count, ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(rt.retained_count, 0) / cs.cohort_size, 2) as retention_percentage FROM cohort_size_calc cs CROSS JOIN retained_2023 rt
results.gold_sql:
WITH first_res AS (
  SELECT client_id, MIN(pickup_date) AS first_pickup
  FROM reservations WHERE status <> 'cancelled'
  GROUP BY client_id),
cohort AS (
  SELECT client_id FROM first_res
  WHERE first_pickup >= DATE '2022-01-01' AND first_pickup < DATE '2023-01-01')
SELECT COUNT(*) AS cohort_size,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE EXISTS (
         SELECT 1 FROM reservations r
         WHERE r.client_id = cohort.client_id AND r.status <> 'cancelled'
           AND r.pickup_date >= DATE '2023-01-01'
           AND r.pickup_date < DATE '2024-01-01')) AS retained,
       ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE EXISTS (
         SELECT 1 FROM reservations r
         WHERE r.client_id = cohort.client_id AND r.status <> 'cancelled'
           AND r.pickup_date >= DATE '2023-01-01'
           AND r.pickup_date < DATE '2024-01-01')) / COUNT(*), 2) AS retention_pct
FROM cohort

results.question: Rank the vehicles by their number of maintenance records, where vehicles with the same count share a rank and no rank numbers are skipped. Show the license plate, the number of maintenance records and the rank, for ranks 1 through 3.
results.sql: WITH ranked_vehicles AS (SELECT v.license_plate, COUNT(mr.id) as maintenance_count, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(mr.id) DESC) as rank FROM vehicles v LEFT JOIN maintenance_records mr ON v.id = mr.vehicle_id GROUP BY v.id, v.license_plate) SELECT license_plate, maintenance_count, rank FROM ranked_vehicles WHERE rank <= 3 ORDER BY rank, maintenance_count DESC, license_plate
results.gold_sql:
SELECT license_plate, maintenance_count, rnk FROM (
  SELECT v.license_plate, COUNT(m.id) AS maintenance_count,
         DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(m.id) DESC) AS rnk
  FROM vehicles v
  JOIN maintenance_records m ON m.vehicle_id = v.id
  GROUP BY v.id, v.license_plate) t
WHERE rnk <= 3

results.question: For each branch, show the branch name, the number of distinct clients who picked up a reservation there in 2023, and the number of distinct clients who picked up a reservation there in 2024, as two separate columns.
results.sql: SELECT l.name AS branch_name, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN EXTRACT(YEAR FROM r.pickup_date) = 2023 THEN r.client_id END) AS clients_2023, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN EXTRACT(YEAR FROM r.pickup_date) = 2024 THEN r.client_id END) AS clients_2024 FROM locations l LEFT JOIN reservations r ON l.id = r.pickup_location GROUP BY l.id, l.name ORDER BY l.name
results.gold_sql:
SELECT l.name,
       COUNT(DISTINCT r.client_id) FILTER (
         WHERE r.pickup_date >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND r.pickup_date < DATE '2024-01-01') AS clients_2023,
       COUNT(DISTINCT r.client_id) FILTER (
         WHERE r.pickup_date >= DATE '2024-01-01' AND r.pickup_date < DATE '2025-01-01') AS clients_2024
FROM locations l LEFT JOIN reservations r ON r.pickup_location = l.id GROUP BY l.name

results.question: What is the longest run of consecutive calendar days on which at least one reservation was picked up at the Downtown Hub branch? Return the length of that run in days as a single number.
results.sql: WITH pickup_dates AS (SELECT DISTINCT r.pickup_date FROM reservations r JOIN locations l ON r.pickup_location = l.id WHERE l.name = 'Downtown Hub' ORDER BY r.pickup_date), dates_with_lag AS (SELECT pickup_date, LAG(pickup_date) OVER (ORDER BY pickup_date) as prev_date, pickup_date - LAG(pickup_date) OVER (ORDER BY pickup_date) as days_since_prev FROM pickup_dates), runs AS (SELECT pickup_date, SUM(CASE WHEN days_since_prev IS NULL OR days_since_prev = 1 THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) OVER (ORDER BY pickup_date) as run_group FROM dates_with_lag), run_lengths AS (SELECT run_group, MIN(pickup_date) as run_start, MAX(pickup_date) as run_end, COUNT(*) as consecutive_days FROM runs GROUP BY run_group) SELECT MAX(consecutive_days) as longest_run FROM run_lengths
results.gold_sql:
WITH d AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT r.pickup_date
  FROM reservations r
  JOIN locations l ON l.id = r.pickup_location
  WHERE l.name = 'Downtown Hub'),
grp AS (
  SELECT pickup_date,
         pickup_date - (ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY pickup_date))::int AS g
  FROM d)
SELECT MAX(len) AS longest_streak FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS len FROM grp GROUP BY g) t

results.question: Which clients have rented vehicles from all five vehicle categories at least once? Show each client's first name and last name.
results.sql: SELECT c.first_name, c.last_name FROM clients c WHERE c.id IN (SELECT r.client_id FROM reservations r JOIN vehicles v ON r.vehicle_id = v.id GROUP BY r.client_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT v.category_id) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT id) FROM vehicle_categories)) ORDER BY c.first_name, c.last_name
results.gold_sql: SELECT c.first_name, c.last_name FROM clients c JOIN reservations r ON r.client_id = c.id JOIN vehicles v ON v.id = r.vehicle_id GROUP BY c.id, c.first_name, c.last_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT v.category_id) = 5

results.question: For each branch, what percentage of the reservations picked up there were cancelled? Show the branch name and the percentage rounded to one decimal.
results.sql: SELECT l.name AS branch_name, ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(CASE WHEN r.status = 'cancelled' THEN 1 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS cancellation_percentage FROM reservations r JOIN locations l ON r.pickup_location = l.id GROUP BY l.id, l.name ORDER BY l.name
results.gold_sql:
SELECT l.name,
       ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE r.status = 'cancelled') / COUNT(*), 1) AS cancelled_pct
FROM reservations r JOIN locations l ON l.id = r.pickup_location GROUP BY l.name

results.question: Which vehicles have cost more in total maintenance than 30 percent of the total revenue from completed payments on their reservations? Show the license plate, the revenue and the maintenance cost.
results.sql: WITH vehicle_maintenance AS (SELECT vehicle_id, SUM(cost) as total_maintenance_cost FROM maintenance_records GROUP BY vehicle_id), vehicle_revenue AS (SELECT v.id, COALESCE(SUM(p.amount), 0) as total_revenue FROM vehicles v LEFT JOIN reservations r ON v.id = r.vehicle_id LEFT JOIN payments p ON r.id = p.reservation_id AND p.status = 'completed' GROUP BY v.id) SELECT v.license_plate, vr.total_revenue as revenue, COALESCE(vm.total_maintenance_cost, 0) as maintenance_cost FROM vehicles v LEFT JOIN vehicle_maintenance vm ON v.id = vm.vehicle_id LEFT JOIN vehicle_revenue vr ON v.id = vr.id WHERE COALESCE(vm.total_maintenance_cost, 0) > 0.30 * vr.total_revenue ORDER BY v.license_plate
results.gold_sql:
WITH rev AS (
  SELECT r.vehicle_id, SUM(p.amount) AS revenue
  FROM payments p
  JOIN reservations r ON r.id = p.reservation_id
  WHERE p.status = 'completed'
  GROUP BY r.vehicle_id),
mnt AS (
  SELECT vehicle_id, SUM(cost) AS maintenance_cost
  FROM maintenance_records
  GROUP BY vehicle_id)
SELECT v.license_plate, rev.revenue, mnt.maintenance_cost FROM rev JOIN mnt ON mnt.vehicle_id = rev.vehicle_id JOIN vehicles v ON v.id = rev.vehicle_id WHERE mnt.maintenance_cost > 0.30 * rev.revenue

results.question: For the vehicle with license plate BDH-1053, show the number of reservations picked up in each month of 2024 - all twelve months, with a zero for months in which it had none. Show the month as a date and the count.
results.sql: WITH months_2024 AS (SELECT generate_series('2024-01-01'::date, '2024-12-01'::date, '1 month'::interval)::date AS month_start), reservations_2024 AS (SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', r.pickup_date)::date AS pickup_month, COUNT(*) AS reservation_count FROM vehicles v JOIN reservations r ON v.id = r.vehicle_id WHERE v.license_plate = 'BDH-1053' AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM r.pickup_date) = 2024 GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', r.pickup_date)::date) SELECT m.month_start AS month, COALESCE(rc.reservation_count, 0) AS count FROM months_2024 m LEFT JOIN reservations_2024 rc ON m.month_start = rc.pickup_month ORDER BY m.month_start
results.gold_sql:
SELECT m.month::date AS month, COUNT(r.id) AS reservations FROM generate_series(DATE '2024-01-01', DATE '2024-12-01', INTERVAL '1 month') AS m(month) LEFT JOIN reservations r
  ON DATE_TRUNC('month', r.pickup_date) = m.month
 AND r.vehicle_id = (SELECT id FROM vehicles WHERE license_plate = 'BDH-1053')
GROUP BY m.month ORDER BY m.month

results.question: Care sucursală a adus cei mai mulți bani în 2024?
results.sql: SELECT l.name as branch_name, l.city, SUM(r.total_cost) as total_revenue FROM reservations r JOIN locations l ON r.pickup_location = l.id WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM r.pickup_date) = 2024 AND r.total_cost IS NOT NULL GROUP BY l.id, l.name, l.city ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 1

results.question: What is our average revenue per client?
results.sql: SELECT AVG(client_revenue) as average_revenue_per_client FROM (SELECT r.client_id, SUM(p.amount) as client_revenue FROM reservations r JOIN payments p ON r.id = p.reservation_id GROUP BY r.client_id) as client_revenues
